LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we read for comprehension?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition
2. respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 6.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 6.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension to a partner. (skill: respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition.
3. Practise this skill: respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we read for comprehension?
2. Why do people take part in economic activities in the society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 6.2.1 Reading for Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary related to the theme from texts for language acquisition.
5. Be able to: respond to comprehension questions from texts on the theme for compression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
